name: Nanbeige4.3-33B
context_scaling: Native 524,288 tokens declared in config.json (max_position_embeddings 524288, rope_theta 1.2e8, rope_scaling null - no YaRN or other extension recipe). The card repeats 'up to 524,288 tokens (512K)' with no long-context eval published.
attention_variant: Standard full GQA on all 52 layers - no linear-attention or sparse layer in the stack, and config.json has no layer_types key. 56 query heads over 8 KV heads (GQA ratio 7) at head_dim 128.
notes:
ADDED 2026-10-26 from the trending sweep (trendingScore rank 3, 474 likes on 0 downloads - released 2026-10-24, two days before this sweep). DENSE, NOT MoE: config.json is model_type llama with no expert/top_k/moe key under any spelling, so active_params_b equals params_b and the whole 33.1B must be resident. params_b 33.119 = safetensors total 33,118,977,024 / 1e9. kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 52 layers x 8 kv_heads x 128 head_dim x 2 (K and V) x 2 bytes (fp16) = 212,992 B/token = 208 KiB/token; at the declared 512K context that is 109 GB of KV alone, so the declared context is not runnable on this user's box and the practical ceiling is far lower (a 32K working context costs 6.8 GB). HARDWARE GATE: passes as written (active 33.1B <= 40, params_b x 0.5 GiB = 16.6 <= 128) but read that generously - bf16 weights are 66 GB and a 4-bit quant is ~17 GB plus KV, so expect a partial offload rather than a clean fit.

WHY IT IS WORTH A RECORD: it is the class leader on 6 of the 19 rows its card prints against ~30B peers, and the card names its comparison set explicitly (Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer-30B, Gemma4-31B) with a harness footnote per row, so the beats are same-test beats. Size-class audit run on 2026-10-26 against every catalog record in the 20-45B band:
BEATS class best - NL2Repo 53.0 vs Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B 46.2; Toolathlon-Verified 70.4 vs Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B 48.7; SWE-Atlas-QnA 50.8 vs Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B 39.8; DeepSWE 65.5 vs VeriLoop E2 64.6; JobBench 44.8 vs Fx-Work 25.19; AA-LCR 84.0 vs Sage-A1.5 81.0.
LOSES where the class already had a stronger entry: SWE-Bench Pro 60.3 vs Recursive Flint 89.7; Scicode 52.6 vs BigBang-v1 68.6; Automation Bench 54.2 vs occamy-1.0 69.1; GDPval 84.8 vs Fx-Work 86.66; Claw-Eval 78.3 vs occamy-1.0 82.2; Tau3-Bench 48.8 vs Xing4.0-29B-A4B 64.63; GPQA Diamond 89.5 vs VeriLoop E2 93.9; AIME 2026 95.2 vs VeriLoop E2 98.3; Terminal-Bench 4.0 23.8 vs VeriLoop E2 37.9.
SETS the class best with no prior row to beat: Terminal-Bench 2.1 80.9 (the two existing 20-45B rows are VeriLoop E2 88.8, a CEILING descriptor row, and Qwen3.8-27B 73.0, so 80.9 sits between non-comparable numbers and gets no verdict), SkillsBench 61.1, DeepPlanning 63.3, EnterpriseOps-Gym 41.0.
Two caveats blunt the wins. VeriLoop E2's 93.9 GPQA / 98.3 AIME / 88.8 Terminal-Bench are self-declared .eval_results rows the catalog already flags as vendor claims with no harness, and Recursive Flint's 89.7 SWE-bench Pro comes from a figure read by eye. The DeepSWE win is 0.9 over a figure read with +/-0.5 error and the two cards do not agree on version (this one prints no version, VeriLoop's row is v1.1). Against clean rows (Qwen3.8-27B, Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, occamy-1.0) the pattern holds: far ahead on agentic cowork and long-context reasoning, behind on pure SWE-style repair.
YC-bench is printed as a dollar return ($1,025,437 vs $641,290 for Qwen3.8-27B) and is NOT transcribed as a benchmark row because its scale is not 100.
NANBEIGE'S OWN FRAMING: the card says this 33B is the teacher for a distillation pipeline into a smaller Nanbeige4.3-3B (not yet released), so a size-class upset here likely repeats at 3B in a later sweep.
